printed_headline_estimate: Conditional logit model of water source choice (N = 1,562 households with >1 option out of 2,190 surveyed households, PDF pp. 6, 8, 11): +1 km distance to public tap at mean distance increases probability of using a well by 43% in urban areas and 27% in rural areas (delta-method SEs in Table 5, PDF p. 24, rendered as non-text image). Reduced-form Tobit model of weekly water collection hours on leave-out mean cluster distance (PDF pp. 12-13): quadratic distance terms jointly significant in rural areas (p = 0.081 adults, p = 0.052 children, PDF p. 12); distance and distance-age interactions jointly significant (p = 0.0061 rural, p = 0.0596 urban, PDF p. 13). No SWiM-eligible exposure tested.
publication_year_note: No publication year, journal name, volume/issue, or copyright date is printed anywhere in the 32-page PDF, which is an undated author manuscript/postprint (survey fielded 2004-2005; latest cited reference is Greene, 2008 on PDF p. 30). Although the prompt's bibliographic header DOI contains '2011', no year appears on the article itself.
rationale: The full text reports two inferential econometric analyses using 2004-2005 household survey data from 73 communities in Madagascar (N = 2,190 households total; N = 1,562 multi-option households in discrete choice): (1) a conditional logit model of household choice among public tap, private tap, well, and surface water, and (2) reduced-form Tobit regressions of individual weekly water-collection hours (Note: Tables 1-6 and A1-A4 on PDF pp. 20-29 have captions only because table bodies are unextracted images, but the prose on pp. 8-13 specifies every regressor and reports marginal effects and joint test p-values). However, all tested predictors are physical infrastructure proximity/availability (distance to sources, leave-out mean cluster distance, source-type availability dummies) and socio-demographic controls (head's age, education, gender, asset index, household age/sex composition, and province dummies). Note 12 (PDF p. 17) explicitly confirms that no tariff/fee, legal tenure, governance, ownership-regulation, or institutional exposure was recorded, so the study fails narrow Criterion 2 and fits no SWiM family.
